one_sentence_story: In 2013 at the University of Rochester, live brain microscopy revealed that entering deep sleep shrinks support cells to widen the spaces between neurons by 60 percent, letting clear fluid flush out sticky amyloid waste twice as fast as when awake.
so_what_for_you: Pulling late nights does not just make you tired — it skips the physical plumbing wash cycle that clears sticky metabolic waste from your cortex during deep early-night sleep.
